summary: SSO claim suffix truncation prevents access to Runbook Lookup (403 on runbooks)
description:
Issue summary: After last-night's IdP attribute transform rollout, many internal users (SRE/oncall) receive 403 when accessing the internal Runbook Lookup UI. Impact: ~40% of oncall and SRE team members could not open runbooks via the portal during the morning shift, slowing incident response and requiring manual sharing of runbook links. Not a customer-facing outage but high internal business impact.

Observed behavior: SSO completes but the Runbook Portal returns 403. Users report 'Access Denied' even though their groups are visible in Okta admin.

Initial timestamps: first report at 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC (internal oncall slack #oncall-alerts). IdP transform rollout window: 2026-03-09 23:50-00:10 UTC.

Important notes: This ticket is focused on access/login mapping (Okta -> Redwood RBAC) rather than network/TLS issues.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Sign in to SSO via Okta for an affected user (example: jdoe@redwood.example)
2) Redirect to Runbook Lookup (/runbooks)
3) Observe 403 Access Denied page in the UI and a 403 from /api/runbooks in the browser devtools.
4) Check /debug/session headers: assertion contains preferred_username without domain (jdoe) while RBAC expects full_email (jdoe@redwood.example).
logs:
auth-proxy: 2026-03-10T02:18:33Z WARN 403 - session:abc123 - mapped_groups=[] - missing_rbac_binding
identity-proxy: 2026-03-10T02:18:32Z INFO idp_assertion: {preferred_username: "jdoe", email: "jdoe@redwood.example"} (note: some assertions show email with domain removed)
okta-audit: 2026-03-09T23:51:10Z UPDATE attributeTransform: stripDomainSuffix=true applied to group devops-rollout
investigation_notes:
Timeline and findings:
- Correlation between Okta attribute transform rollout and first reports.
- Reproduced locally by forcing an assertion where preferred_username != email. Runbook Portal's RBAC matching uses the email identity key; identity-proxy was normalizing to preferred_username when stripDomainSuffix=true.
- Audit of Okta -> Saw a new expression mapping that strips '@redwood.example' for users with multi-alias accounts. A subset of users had their assertion include the username without domain which fails exact-match RBAC.
- Temporary mitigation verified: adding an alternate_identity mapping in identity-proxy to map preferred_username back to the email allowed access.
- No evidence of group membership loss in Okta; groups are present but RBAC grant code path short-circuits when primary identifier mismatches.
- Related code path: identity-proxy v2.14.1 uses identity_key precedence: preferred_username -> email. That is usually fine but the transform removed the domain from preferred_username making it ambiguous.

Hypothesis: The Okta transform was overly aggressive (stripDomainSuffix) for users with multiple aliases, causing the identity key used by RBAC to mismatch and return no bindings.
root_cause: A recent Okta attribute transform (stripDomainSuffix=true) was rolled out to a subset of groups. For affected accounts the IdP assertion's preferred_username lost the domain suffix, which caused our RBAC matching to fail because the service relied on the full email address. The transform was applied without a corresponding identity-proxy normalization change or a fallback to email, causing a regression across runbook access flows.
resolution:
Workaround and rollback: At 2026-03-12 07:20 UTC we rolled back the Okta attribute transform for the devops rollout group and applied a short-term identity-proxy config change to accept both preferred_username and email as candidate identity keys. Access verified restored for affected users by 2026-03-12 07:45 UTC.

Permanent remediation: 1) Identity team to ship identity-proxy change to normalize and prefer full email when present (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1243). 2) Add e2e tests that cover Okta transform variants and RBAC matching logic. 3) Update runbook-portal docs to list accepted identity claim keys. 4) Coordinate any future Okta transforms with identity and SRE (runbook: INT-135791 created for follow-up automation).
resolution_notes:
Rollback of Okta transform completed; identity-proxy hotfix applied to staging then prod. Verified via synthetic login checks and oncall user confirmations. Created follow-up tasks: update tests, add monitoring alert on sudden drop in runbook portal RBAC matches, and add an Okta pre-rollout checklist for attribute changes.

ETA for permanent fix: identity-proxy normalization patch targeted for 2026-03-19 release window.

Status: Access restored, monitoring in place.

2026-03-10 03:22 - Diego Morales (SRE): Reproduced locally with injected assertion. RBAC returns empty bindings because identifier mismatch. Temporary workaround: add alternate_identity mapping in identity-proxy config (manual).
2026-03-12 07:25 - Diego Morales (SRE): Rolled back transform in Okta for the rollout group. Confirmed multiple users can access runbooks again. Will follow up with permanent code change.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Aisha Patel (Reporter): Confirmed access restored for oncall shift. Thanks team. Leaving ticket open for follow-up and tests.
